Unit 6 - Paired Passages — Title & Goal
Learn to master unit 6 - paired passages questions for the Digital SAT through a short concept, a modeled item, and targeted practice.

Key skill

Read the note and focus on what the question is really asking inside the passage.

  • Locate explicit claims and implicit ideas.
  • Ask: What is the passage mainly doing?
  • Match answers to the most general accurate statement.

Model item

Study how the evidence in the passage supports the correct answer.

Passage 1 — The scientist argues urban trees lower temperatures.
Passage 2 — A planner claims benefits are overstated without watering plans.

Question 1. How does Passage 2 respond to Passage 1?

  • It supports Passage 1 with new data.
  • It challenges Passage 1 by raising practical concerns.
  • It ignores Passage 1.
  • It repeats Passage 1's examples.
Practical implementation concern → challenges → B.

Quick practice

Try these quickly. Eliminate two choices before choosing your answer.

Both passages discuss city shade programs.

Question 2. Which choice identifies a point of agreement?

  • Trees provide no benefit.
  • Shade has some cooling effect.
  • Watering is unnecessary.
  • Cities should remove trees.

Next skill

Build on the previous skill. Compare how this question type reads the passage differently.

Note: Locate the exact phrase or sentence that proves your choice.

Another model item

Notice how small wording differences change the best answer.

Passage 1 suggests pocket parks; Passage 2 suggests rooftop gardens.

Question 3. Which choice best describes the relationship?

  • Contradictory conclusions
  • Alternative solutions to a shared goal
  • No connection
  • Identical plans

More practice

Aim for accuracy first, then speed. Re-check the evidence that rules out each wrong choice.

Passage 1 — volunteers planted trees; Passage 2 — volunteers monitored soil moisture.

Question 4. Which choice best synthesizes the passages’ approaches?

  • Competing outcomes
  • Sequential phases of a shared project
  • Unrelated hobbies
  • Exclusive methods

Mixed practice set

These mix multiple skills. Mark the question type before you start, then solve.

Passage 1 touts immediate shade; Passage 2 warns of long-term maintenance.

Question 5. Which choice captures both perspectives?

  • Immediate benefits without drawbacks
  • Benefits exist, but maintenance planning matters
  • No benefits exist
  • Maintenance is irrelevant
